title: scan result
description: A page of lines holding a literal or matching a pattern, with counts, a time-budget stop and a cursor.

request.description: The request echoed with defaults filled in (roots is null when not given).

case.description: The case requested (case_applied says what smart resolved to).

roots.description: Root ids to search. Narrows the server's roots, never widens them; absent or null means every root the server allows.

name_glob.description: Matched against the file name (the last path component): * is any run of code points, ? one code point, every other code point itself; case-sensitive; no /.

context_lines.description: Lines of context before and after each hit.

max_hits_per_file.description: At most this many hit lines from one file; files_capped counts files that had more.

cursor.description: The previous page's next_cursor. One from another generation (or another walk of the folder) is refused as a stale cursor, one from another request as not belonging to this request.

time_budget_ms.description: How long this page may search, in milliseconds; a page that runs out ends with stopped time and a cursor to continue.

source.description: What was scanned: an index, or a folder with nothing prepared (searchd scan --folder).

generation.description: The index generation this answer came from; null for a folder.

warnings.description: Warnings about this answer: pattern_matches_empty when the pattern can match the empty string (a line can then match with no match_offsets).

case_applied.description: The case that applied (what smart resolved to).

hits.description: This page's hit lines, by root_id, path (bytes) and line.

files_matched.description: Files with a hit, among those whose scan ended on this page; summed over pages, the total.

files_scanned.description: Files searched to their end on this page; summed over pages, the total.

files_capped.description: Files with more hit lines than max_hits_per_file, among those whose scan ended on this page.

bytes_scanned.description: Bytes of the files counted in files_scanned.

pending_files.description: Files in scope still waiting for their bytes (an index; 0 for a folder); the corpus may be incomplete when above 0.

not_scanned.description: Files in scope that could not be searched, by reason. An index: scope-wide, the same on every page. A folder: counted on the page that reached the file.

unreadable.description: Could not be read (or its retained bytes failed their check).

budget_exhausted.description: Not indexed in full because the indexing byte budget ran out.

not_retained.description: Indexed in a root that keeps no source bytes.

not_read.description: A folder: the walk's files not read, counted by kind (only kinds with a count); null for an index. These do not set truncated.

truncated.description: True when the corpus may be incomplete: pending_files above 0 or a not_scanned count above 0. It is not about paging.

stopped.description: time: the page ran out of time_budget_ms; next_cursor continues it and is never null.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page; null when the scan reached the end of the last file.

scope.description: The scope the request ran in.

roots.description: The root ids the request could see, in the generation's order.

labels_applied.description: Always true: the scope's labels (possibly none) filtered before any candidate. It does not say whether labels hid anything.

line.description: Line number (1-based; a leading BOM is not part of line 1), as read_span numbers lines.

text.description: The line without its terminator, at most 512 bytes (cut at a code-point boundary); in regex mode shorter when the line has more than 16 non-empty matches starting within it, ending where the 17th starts (matches_truncated).

text_truncated.description: True when text is shorter than the line (the 512-byte cut or the cut at the 17th match).

matches_truncated.description: Regex mode: true when text was cut where a 17th non-empty match starts, so the line holds more matches than match_offsets lists (empty matches are not listed and do not count). False when only the 512-byte cut applies, and always false in literal mode, which lists every match.

match_offsets.description: Match ranges [start, end) in code points into text: non-empty matches only, those starting within text, ends clipped to text.

before.description: Up to context_lines lines before the hit.

after.description: Up to context_lines lines after the hit.

text.description: The line without its terminator, at most 512 bytes (cut at a code-point boundary).

text_truncated.description: True when text is shorter than the line.
